clue.text: This selling to boost Egypt's economy?

definitions.text: This selling to boost Egypt's economy

parts.words: This selling to boost Egypt's economy
parts.note: the question pretends Egypt's monuments are being sold off

explanation.surface: A question about some sales drive meant to prop up the Egyptian economy.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is a pun: the kind of selling named is a fraudulent chain scheme, and Egypt's best-known structures share its name.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyramid selling is a multi-level marketing fraud, and the tombs at Giza give the joke its Egyptian setting.

clue.text: Member enters huge building or small excrescence

indicators.note: enters means the member goes inside the building

parts.note: a pile is a large imposing building
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician walks into a great building, or a small growth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' is the UK convention for MP.
explanation.definitionFit: A pimple is a small spot on the skin, an example of a little outgrowth.

clue.text: Change one's course about true love perhaps

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters given may be arranged in another way

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Someone changes direction over a matter of real romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' signals a rearrangement of the word true together with the letter for love; 'love' as O comes from the tennis score.
explanation.definitionFit: To reroute is to send along a different path, a synonym.

clue.text: Was On Liberty as explosive as this ?

definitions.text: Was On Liberty as explosive as this

parts.words: Was On Liberty as explosive as this
parts.note: On Liberty is the essay by J S Mill, so the question asks whether that philosopher's work was as explosive as his own hand grenade

explanation.surface: A question about whether a famous essay was a bombshell.
explanation.walkthrough: On Liberty is by John Stuart Mill, so the essay is Mill's bomb; the Mills bomb was a British hand grenade.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mills bomb was a British hand grenade of the World Wars, punningly the philosopher's own explosive.

clue.text: Insight in troubles of 100 miners, in depression

indicators.note: the second in places the scrambled letters within the hollow

parts.note: a dent is a hollow or depression

indicators.note: troubles means disturbs, so the letters are stirred up

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: An understanding of the troubles of a hundred miners during a slump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubles' signals the mixing of C with the miners; 'in' (the second one) places that mixture inside the hollow. 'depression' looks like an economic slump but is a dent.
explanation.definitionFit: Discernment is keen perception or judgement, a synonym.

clue.text: Flower, one of two the grass may go between

definitions.text: one of two the grass may go between

explanation.surface: A flower described as something grass might pass between.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer as COW'S LIP: grass being eaten goes between a cow's two lips.
explanation.definitionFit: The cowslip is a yellow spring primula; read as a cow's lip, it is one of the pair a grazing cow takes grass between.

clue.text: What takes men to the opera ?

definitions.text: What takes men to the opera

parts.words: What takes men to the opera
parts.note: a vehicle carries people to a show, and the same word followed by men spells Bizet's opera

explanation.surface: A question about how the gentlemen get to the opera house.
explanation.walkthrough: The word plus MEN makes CARMEN, Bizet's opera, as well as being the vehicle that drives men there.
explanation.definitionFit: A motor vehicle carries passengers, and put before men it names Bizet's opera.

clue.text: West has, sound marine source of oil

parts.note: hale means healthy, sound in body

explanation.surface: A Western country has a sound supply of oil from the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' is the adjective meaning healthy, not a sign of something heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Whales were hunted for their blubber, which was boiled down into lamp oil.

clue.text: Reduce one's burden, and one's gloom

explanation.surface: Ease a load and cheer up at the same time.
explanation.definitionFit: Lighten means make less heavy, and also make brighter or more cheerful.

clue.text: Like the bars that provide no meeting-places

definitions.text: Like the bars that provide no meeting-places

parts.words: Like the bars that provide no meeting-places
parts.note: gymnastic bars of this kind run side by side, and such lines never meet, so the bars are no place for a rendezvous

explanation.surface: A description of pubs where nobody can get together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bars' suggests pubs, but these are the gymnast's pair of bars, and lines of this kind never meet.
explanation.definitionFit: Parallel bars are gymnastics apparatus, and parallel lines by definition never meet.

clue.text: Harpagon holds an exam for eg Alice's Duchess

indicators.note: the miser holds the exam inside him, so one word is placed within the other

parts.note: Harpagon is the money-hoarding hero of Moliere's play The Miser
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A Moliere character sits an exam to qualify for some role in Wonderland.
explanation.walkthrough: The Duchess in Alice in Wonderland keeps finding a moral in everything, which makes her the example.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Carroll's Duchess declares that everything has a moral, the habit of a preacher of lessons.

clue.text: A guru confounded by a soothsayer

indicators.note: confounded means thrown into confusion, so the letters of the two words are mixed up

explanation.surface: A spiritual teacher left baffled by a fortune-teller.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman augur foretold events from the flight of birds, the work of a prophet.

clue.text: King of the ring

explanation.surface: Someone crowned champion of the boxing ring.
explanation.walkthrough: France had eighteen kings of this name, and Joe Louis was world heavyweight boxing champion; the ring is the boxing ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Many French monarchs bore the name, and the boxer Joe Louis held the heavyweight title for twelve years.

clue.text: Spirit makes poor Lee unbalanced

indicators.note: poor here suggests something botched or badly made, so the name's letters are rearranged

parts.note: unbalanced in the sense of mentally disturbed, a slang sense of mental

explanation.surface: Someone called Lee is said to be driven mad by a ghost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges LEE as ELE.
explanation.definitionFit: An elemental is a nature spirit of folklore, one of earth, air, fire or water.

clue.text: It copied sepia reproduction on a screen

definitions.text: It copied sepia reproduction on a screen

indicators.note: a reproduction is a fresh version made from the original, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A projector reproduces old brown-toned photographs onto a screen.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a device that projects pictures, including opaque prints, onto a screen.
explanation.definitionFit: An epidiascope is a projector that throws images of both slides and opaque pages onto a screen.

clue.text: Direct course into artistic revival — job for a scout

indicators.note: into says the one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the Renaissance was the revival of art and learning in Europe
to con a ship is to direct its course from the bridge

explanation.surface: Instructions to steer a course straight into an art revival, then a scout's task.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Direct' looks like an adjective; to con is the nautical verb for steering a ship, and 'into' puts it within the art movement's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Scouting means surveying ground ahead for information, which is exactly a military survey of that kind.

clue.text: Soldiers upset over character of subscription

indicators.note: over places the first piece above the second in this down entry
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word reads upwards

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers
nature means one's character

explanation.surface: Disgruntled troops complain about the character of a subscription.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns GIS into SIG; 'over' puts it above NATURE in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A subscription in the old sense is a name written at the foot of a document, a synonym.

clue.text: Neat hand

explanation.surface: A tidy hand of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: Neat spirits are drunk without water; a straight is a poker hand of five cards in sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirits taken neat are undiluted, and in poker a run of five consecutive cards is a ranked hand.

clue.text: Sleight-of-hand needed to attach tackle to cover of a sewer

parts.note: a sewer here is one who sews, whose fingertip is covered by a thimble
a ship's rigging is its tackle of ropes and chains

explanation.surface: A conjuring trick that involves fixing gear onto a drain cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sewer' is not a drain but a person sewing. The count (6-7) is missing from the clue as held. Thimblerigging is the shell game: a pea hidden under one of three cups.
explanation.definitionFit: The thimblerig is a cheating game where a pea is shuffled under cups, a classic trick by a conjuror's nimble fingers.

clue.text: Drive to hold the island state thus put in jeopardy

indicators.note: to hold means the drive contains the state's letters

parts.note: to impel is to drive forward
RI is Rhode Island, a US state

explanation.surface: An effort to drive back and hold an island nation puts it at risk.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhode Island, abbreviated RI, is the smallest US state, despite not being an island as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: To imperil is to endanger, a synonym.

clue.text: Arresting: for 'theft.

explanation.surface: Making an arrest for stealing.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are British slang: the police nick a suspect, and to nick is to steal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nick is British slang both for arresting a person and for stealing something.

clue.text: Wild woman of the West, and frenzied

parts.note: Mae West was the Hollywood actress

indicators.note: frenzied means wildly excited, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A wild frontier woman of the Old West, in a frenzy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the West' suggests the frontier but is the film star Mae West; 'frenzied' rearranges AND as NAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A maenad was a frenzied female follower of Bacchus, so a crazed woman.

clue.text: A mongrel pup's caught a rat in the equipment

indicators.note: the scrambled pup has caught a rat, so it holds those letters inside
a mongrel is of mixed breed, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: the word pups, with the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A crossbred puppy has caught a rat inside some gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mongrel' mixes the puppies' letters, and 'caught' sets the rat inside them; the opening A stands as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparatus is a set of tools or gear for a task, a synonym.

clue.text: How a Thespian might — to an encore?

definitions.text: How a Thespian might — to an encore

parts.words: How a Thespian might — to an encore
parts.note: an encore calls an actor to perform again, so the actor would respond by acting again

explanation.surface: A question about an actor's response to calls for more.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as RE-ACT, the answer is acting again, which an actor does on an encore, and also responding.
explanation.definitionFit: To react is to respond, and split it reads act again, as an actor does for an encore.

clue.text: If leaving Africa, many invested for this capital return

indicators.note: return means the letters built so far are turned back to front
invested means placed inside, as money is put into a fund
leaving means those two letters depart from the continent's name

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, taken as many

explanation.surface: Advice on moving money out of Africa into an investment that pays a return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes I and F from AFRICA to give ARCA; 'invested' puts C inside as ARCCA; 'return' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Accra is the capital city of Ghana.

clue.text: A hard pull back to the lake

indicators.note: back means the two pieces together are read in reverse

parts.note: to drag is to pull something heavy with effort

explanation.surface: A strenuous haul back to the waterside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns A DRAG round as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Garda is the largest lake in Italy.

clue.text: Favouring one kind of bomb in super-abundance

parts.note: pro means in favour of
a fusion bomb is a hydrogen bomb

explanation.surface: Someone in favour of a nuclear weapon, in great quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: Profusion means a lavish abundance, a synonym.

clue.text: Such dirt should be more profitable 'than crime

definitions.text: Such dirt should be more profitable 'than crime

parts.words: Such dirt should be more profitable 'than crime
parts.note: rich mining ground has a name meaning profit, and the saying goes that crime does not do this

explanation.surface: A remark that honest digging beats crime as a source of money.
explanation.walkthrough: Pay dirt is earth rich in gold, and the proverb says crime doesn't pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Pay dirt is gold-bearing ground; the word also means bring in money, which crime proverbially fails to do.

clue.text: Author whose story has no right to left opening

indicators.note: has no means the letter goes missing from the word

explanation.surface: A writer whose tale lacks a right-hand opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no' removes the right from the tale, and 'opening' places to plus left at the front of what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo Tolstoy was the Russian novelist who wrote War and Peace.

clue.text: University grant backing many went in, came out

indicators.note: went in says the one letter enters the other piece
backing means the word is turned to run backwards

parts.note: a degree is what a university grants
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, taken as many

explanation.surface: Many students went into university once the grant was backed, then came out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns DEGREE into EERGED, and M goes in after the first E.
explanation.definitionFit: To emerge is to come out into view, a synonym.
